## Overview

Package desktop gives a Tela app the services of the desktop it runs on (ADR-178, ADR-181): file and folder dialogs, message boxes, notifications, a tray icon, the app's own folders, a settings store and windows that open where the user left them. It works the same on Linux (Wayland and X11, through the XDG Desktop Portal and the freedesktop D-Bus services) and Windows, and in the headless backend of telatest and tela snapshot.

### Dialogs

[`OpenFile`](#func-openfile), [`OpenFiles`](#func-openfiles), [`SaveFile`](#func-savefile) and [`PickFolder`](#func-pickfolder) show the OS's dialogs; [`Title`](#func-title), [`Directory`](#func-directory), [`DefaultName`](#func-defaultname), [`Filter`](#func-filter) and [`Parent`](#func-parent) configure them. [`ShowMessage`](#func-showmessage) shows a message box with a fixed set of buttons: the OS's on Windows, drawn by Tela with the app's theme on Linux, whose portal has none. They are asynchronous like a browser's APIs: the call returns at once, and the callback runs later on the UI thread, so it may set state. Cancel is not an error: a dialog answers "" (or nil paths) and a nil error.

```go
Button(OnClick(func() {
    desktop.OpenFile(func(path string, err error) {
        if err == nil && path != "" {
            setPath.Set(path)
        }
    }, desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt"))
}), Text("Open…"))
```

The calls run on the UI thread: from event handlers and effects, or from a goroutine through tela.Post. The dialog is modal to the window the call comes from ([`Parent`](#func-parent) chooses another).

### Notifications and the tray

[`Notify`](#func-notify) shows a notification whose OnClick, action and OnClose callbacks run on the UI thread. [`Tray`](#type-tray) is a component: the icon is in the tray while it is mounted and follows its fields, like any other element; its [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem) values run OnSelect. With App.OnClose hiding the main window, the app lives in the tray until tela.Quit.

### Folders, settings and window placement

[`ConfigDir`](#func-configdir), [`DataDir`](#func-datadir), [`CacheDir`](#func-cachedir), [`StateDir`](#func-statedir) and [`LogDir`](#func-logdir) return the app's folders, following each OS's conventions (XDG on Linux, %APPDATA% and %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, \~/Library on macOS), named after the app ID ([`SetAppID`](#func-setappid), else App.AppID, else the executable) and created on demand. [`Store`](#type-store) is a small JSON key-value file written atomically; [`Settings`](#func-settings) is the app's, and [`UseSetting`](#func-usesetting) is a useState whose value lives there:

```go
theme, setTheme := desktop.UseSetting("theme", "system")
```

[`PersistApp`](#func-persistapp) makes the main window open where it was closed; [`SavedWindow`](#type-savedwindow) does the same for a tela.Window, and [`LoadPlacement`](#func-loadplacement) with [`UseSavePlacement`](#func-usesaveplacement) are the parts they are made of.

### Clipboard, shortcuts, launches, registration, secrets, menus and the trash

[`ReadClipboard`](#func-readclipboard) and [`WriteClipboard`](#func-writeclipboard) copy and paste a tela.DataTransfer (text, HTML, images, files, custom types). [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut) is a component that registers a system-wide shortcut while mounted. [`SingleInstance`](#func-singleinstance) keeps one process per app: a second start hands its [`Launch`](#type-launch) to the first, whose [`UseLaunch`](#func-uselaunch) handlers open its files and links. [`Register`](#func-register) makes the app a handler of a [`URLScheme`](#func-urlscheme) or a [`FileType`](#func-filetype) for the user, without a running app too (an installer); [`MakeDefault`](#func-makedefault) is a separate, explicit request. [`SetSecret`](#func-setsecret), [`Secret`](#func-secret) and [`DeleteSecret`](#func-deletesecret) keep small secrets in the OS's keyring, from a goroutine. [`PopupMenu`](#func-popupmenu) and [`MenuBar`](#type-menubar) are the OS's menus where it has them, for kit's menus to use. [`AppMenuBar`](#type-appmenubar) is the app's one menu bar (macOS's, or every framed window's on Windows), and a [`Role`](#type-role) marks a [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem) as a standard one (Copy, the Edit menu) that the OS or this package performs. [`MoveToTrash`](#func-movetotrash) moves a file where the user can restore it, never deleting it, also from a goroutine.

### When a service is missing

Not every desktop has every service: GNOME shows no tray icons without an extension, a minimal Linux session may have no portal (no file dialogs) and no notification daemon. The calls then return an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) (errors.Is), and the app falls back: a path field instead of a dialog, a message in the window instead of a notification, a window that does not hide itself on close without a tray.

### Tests

telatest answers dialogs (App.AnswerFileDialog, App.AnswerMessage), reads and clicks notifications and the tray (App.Notifications, App.ClickNotification, App.Tray, App.ClickTrayItem), and points the folders at a temporary directory (telatest.TempDesktopDirs, which sets the [`DirEnv`](#constants) variable).

## Constants

```go
const DirEnv = "TELA_DESKTOP_DIR"
```

DirEnv is the environment variable that moves every app directory under one folder, for tests and portable installs: with TELA_DESKTOP_DIR=/tmp/x, [`ConfigDir`](#func-configdir) is /tmp/x/\<app ID\>/config, and likewise data, cache, state and logs. telatest.TempDesktopDirs sets it to a temporary folder for one test.

```go
const MainWindowKey = "main"
```

MainWindowKey is the key [`PersistApp`](#func-persistapp) saves the main window's placement under.

```go
const MaxSecretSize = platform.MaxSecretSize
```

MaxSecretSize is the largest secret, in bytes, every OS stores (the limit of the Windows Credential Manager). Keep keys and tokens in secrets; encrypt larger data with a key kept there.

## Variables

```go
var ErrAppNotRegistered = platform.ErrAppNotRegistered
```

ErrAppNotRegistered is wrapped by the error a [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut) reports (ShortcutFailed) when the desktop refused the app's ID: on Linux the GlobalShortcuts portal (xdg-desktop-portal 1.22) accepts an app only when the desktop has an entry for its ID ([`AppID`](#func-appid) + ".desktop"), which [`RegisterApp`](#func-registerapp) writes. The error names the entry. On X11 the shortcut is grabbed instead and works without one.

```go
var ErrAssociationTaken = platform.ErrAssociationTaken
```

ErrAssociationTaken is wrapped by the error of [`Register`](#func-register) when another application holds the association and [`Replace`](#func-replace) was not given; nothing was written. The error names the other application.

```go
var ErrDevExecutable = errors.New("under tela dev the program is a temporary build; give the installed program's path with desktop.ForApp(desktop.HandlerApp{Exec: ...}) " +
    "(on macOS, the program inside the .app that `tela build` writes), or register from a program started with `tela run`")
```

ErrDevExecutable is wrapped by the error of [`Register`](#func-register) and [`MakeDefault`](#func-makedefault) under tela dev when no Exec was given (ForApp): the running program is a temporary dev build, which the OS must not be told to run. Nothing is written. Give the installed program's path, or register from a normal build.

```go
var ErrSecretCanceled = platform.ErrSecretCanceled
```

ErrSecretCanceled is returned by the secret functions when the user canceled the OS's prompt to unlock the keyring (Linux): nothing was read or written. Asking again later is fine; do not ask in a loop.

```go
var ErrSecretNotFound = platform.ErrSecretNotFound
```

ErrSecretNotFound is returned by [`Secret`](#func-secret) when no secret has the name. errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) also holds.

```go
var ErrSecretTooLarge = platform.ErrSecretTooLarge
```

ErrSecretTooLarge is returned by [`SetSecret`](#func-setsecret) for a secret larger than MaxSecretSize.

```go
var ErrUnsupported = fmt.Errorf("desktop: %w", errors.ErrUnsupported)
```

ErrUnsupported is wrapped by the errors of services the platform or the session does not provide: file dialogs without an XDG Desktop Portal, a tray icon without a StatusNotifierWatcher (some GNOME sessions), any service on a backend that has none. Test for it with errors.Is and fall back:

```go
err := desktop.OpenFile(onPicked, desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md"))
if errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
    showPathField() // let the user type a path instead
}
```

errors.Is(err, errors.ErrUnsupported) holds too.

## Functions

### func AppID

```go
func AppID() string
```

AppID returns the name of the app's directories: [`SetAppID`](#func-setappid)'s, else the running app's tela.App.AppID, else the executable's name (as the platform's default AppID). Safe from any goroutine.

### func CacheDir

```go
func CacheDir() (string, error)
```

CacheDir returns the app's folder for data it can download or compute again (thumbnails, downloads), creating it if needed. The OS or the user may empty it:

- Linux: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/\<app ID\> (\~/.cache/\<app ID\>)
- Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\\\<app ID\>\\cache
- macOS: \~/Library/Caches/\<app ID\>

### func ClipboardTypes

```go
func ClipboardTypes(done func(types []string, err error)) error
```

ClipboardTypes calls done, later, on the UI thread, with the types the clipboard offers (MIME types, best first), without reading the data: enough to enable a Paste button. Same rules as [`ReadClipboard`](#func-readclipboard).

### func ConfigDir

```go
func ConfigDir() (string, error)
```

ConfigDir returns the app's folder for configuration and settings, creating it if needed:

- Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/\<app ID\> (\~/.config/\<app ID\>)
- Windows: %APPDATA%\\\<app ID\> (roaming)
- macOS: \~/Library/Application Support/\<app ID\>

The app ID is [`AppID`](#func-appid)'s. [`DirEnv`](#constants) moves every directory for tests.

### func DataDir

```go
func DataDir() (string, error)
```

DataDir returns the app's folder for documents and data the user would miss (a library, a database), creating it if needed:

- Linux: $XDG_DATA_HOME/\<app ID\> (\~/.local/share/\<app ID\>)
- Windows: %APPDATA%\\\<app ID\> (roaming; the same as ConfigDir)
- macOS: \~/Library/Application Support/\<app ID\> (the same as ConfigDir)

### func DeleteSecret

```go
func DeleteSecret(name string) error
```

DeleteSecret removes the secret stored under name for this app; a missing one is not an error. It blocks; see [`SetSecret`](#func-setsecret).

### func FlushAll

```go
func FlushAll() error
```

FlushAll writes the changes of every open store ([`Store.Flush`](#func-store-flush)) and returns the first error. tela.Run calls it when it returns.

### func LoadPlacement

```go
func LoadPlacement(key string) tela.WindowPlacement
```

LoadPlacement returns the window placement saved under key (by [`UseSavePlacement`](#func-usesaveplacement) or [`SavePlacement`](#func-saveplacement)), or the zero placement when none was saved: give it to tela.App.Placement or tela.Window.Placement, and the window opens where the user left it. Safe from any goroutine, before tela.Run too (call [`SetAppID`](#func-setappid) first, or use [`PersistApp`](#func-persistapp)).

### func LogDir

```go
func LogDir() (string, error)
```

LogDir returns the app's folder for log files, creating it if needed:

- Linux: $XDG_STATE_HOME/\<app ID\>/logs
- Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\\\<app ID\>\\logs
- macOS: \~/Library/Logs/\<app ID\>

### func MessagePreview

```go
func MessagePreview(m Message) tela.Component
```

MessagePreview is the drawn message box of m as a component, without a window: what the box shows on Linux. tela snapshot renders it in a preview (the window is 440 pixels wide), and a test can mount it:

```go
func Preview() tela.Component {
    return desktop.MessagePreview(desktop.Message{Kind: desktop.MessageWarning, Text: "Disk almost full."})
}
```

Its buttons do nothing.

### func MoveToTrash

```go
func MoveToTrash(path string) error
```

MoveToTrash moves the file or folder at path to the user's trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows, the Trash of the Linux desktop), where the user can restore it. A relative path is taken from the working directory. It never deletes: when the trash cannot take the file (a desktop without one, a file on a network drive or on another disk than the trash), the file stays where it is and the error wraps [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables), so the app can tell the user the file is still there. A path that does not exist is an error wrapping fs.ErrNotExist.

Ask the user first, and call it from a goroutine: it blocks on file I/O and the desktop's file operation, and dev mode warns when it runs on the UI thread.

```go
go func() {
    err := desktop.MoveToTrash(path)
    tela.Post(func() {
        switch {
        case err == nil:
            toast.Show("Moved " + filepath.Base(path) + " to the Trash")
        case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported):
            toast.Show("The file is still in " + filepath.Dir(path))
        default:
            toast.Error("Could not move the file", kit.ToastDescription(err.Error()))
        }
    })
}()
```

It needs a running app (tela.Run or telatest). In tests, telatest's headless trash moves the file into a temporary folder and App.Trashed lists what went there; App.FailTrash and App.Unsupported(telatest.Trash) play the failures.

### func OpenFile

```go
func OpenFile(done func(path string, err error), opts ...DialogOption) error
```

OpenFile shows the OS's open-file dialog and calls done with the chosen file. A path of "" with a nil error means the user canceled:

```go
desktop.OpenFile(func(path string, err error) {
    switch {
    case err != nil:
        setError(err.Error())
    case path == "":
        // canceled
    default:
        load(path)
    }
}, desktop.Title("Open a note"), desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt"))
```

Call it on the UI thread: an event handler or an effect (from a goroutine, wrap it in tela.Post). It returns at once; done runs later on the UI thread, exactly once, so it may set state. The returned error says the dialog could not be shown, and done is then never called: no running app, or a desktop without file dialogs (errors.Is(err, [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables)): on Linux, no XDG Desktop Portal). Tests answer the dialog with telatest's App.AnswerFileDialog.

**Example**

An open button: the dialog answers on the UI thread, and a desktop without file dialogs falls back to a path field.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    path, setPath := tela.UseState("")
    typing, setTyping := tela.UseState(false)
    open := func() {
        err := desktop.OpenFile(func(p string, err error) {
            if err == nil && p != "" { // "" is cancel
                setPath.Set(p)
            }
        }, desktop.Title("Open a note"), desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt"))
        if errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
            setTyping.Set(true) // no portal: let the user type the path
        }
    }
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(open), Text("Open…")),
        If(typing, Input(Bind(path, setPath))),
        Text(path),
    )
})
```

### func OpenFiles

```go
func OpenFiles(done func(paths []string, err error), opts ...DialogOption) error
```

OpenFiles is [`OpenFile`](#func-openfile) for several files: done receives the chosen paths, nil when the user canceled.

### func ParseKeys

```go
func ParseKeys(keys string) (string, error)
```

ParseKeys checks a key combination as [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut).Keys takes it and returns it written the usual way, as menus show it (the text for [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem).Accelerator): modifiers then the key, joined by '+'.

```go
desktop.ParseKeys("ctrl+alt+n")   // "Ctrl+Alt+N", nil
desktop.ParseKeys("Ctrl+Hyper+N") // error: "Hyper" is not a modifier
```

Names ignore case. Modifiers: Ctrl (Control), Alt (Option), Shift, Super (Meta, Win, Cmd), and CmdOrCtrl (Super on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). The key comes last: one character ("N", "1", "/"; Shift is written as a modifier), a key name ("F1"…"F24", "Escape", "Enter", "Tab", "Space", "Backspace", "Delete", "Insert", "Home", "End", "PageUp", "PageDown", "ArrowUp" or "Up", "PrintScreen", "MediaPlayPause"…), or "Plus" for '+'.

### func PerformRole

```go
func PerformRole(w tela.WindowHandle, r Role)
```

PerformRole carries out the item role r in window w, as package desktop does for a native menu whose platform only reports the choice: RoleMinimize, RoleZoom and RoleClose act on w, and the edit roles send the element of w that has the focus the role's shortcut (Ctrl+C, or Command+C under the Mac key flavor), so a text field cuts, copies, pastes, undoes and selects all as it does for the keys. It is for menus that Tela draws, such as kit's menus with a Role item: call it from a handler or an effect once the menu has closed and the focus is back on the element the command is for. RoleNone and the menu roles (RoleEditMenu, RoleWindowMenu, RoleHelpMenu) do nothing; so do the edit roles in a tree without a running app (tela snapshot).

### func PersistApp

```go
func PersistApp(app tela.App) tela.App
```

PersistApp returns app with the main window's placement remembered: the placement saved under [`MainWindowKey`](#constants) becomes App.Placement (unless it is set), and the root saves it while the app runs and when it quits. A position saved on a monitor that is gone at the next start opens on the nearest monitor present (telatest.Monitors plays it in tests). When app.AppID is set and [`SetAppID`](#func-setappid) was not called, it names the app's directories ([`SetAppID`](#func-setappid)), so the placement is read before tela.Run from the same folder it is saved to.

```go
func main() {
    tela.Main(desktop.PersistApp(tela.App{
        AppID: "com.example.notes",
        Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 640,
        Root:  Notes{},
    }))
}
```

**Example**

The main window opens where the user left it.

```go
app := desktop.PersistApp(tela.App{
    AppID: "com.example.notes",
    Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 640,
    Root: tela.C(func() tela.Node { return Text("Notes") }),
})
_ = app // tela.Main(app)
```

### func PickFolder

```go
func PickFolder(done func(path string, err error), opts ...DialogOption) error
```

PickFolder shows the OS's folder chooser and calls done with the chosen folder ("" with a nil error: canceled). Same rules as [`OpenFile`](#func-openfile); filters do not apply.

### func PopupMenu

```go
func PopupMenu(w tela.WindowHandle, at tela.Point, items []MenuItem, done func(chosen bool, err error)) error
```

PopupMenu shows items as the OS's context menu of w's window, with its top-left corner at at (logical pixels in the window's coordinates, such as a pointer event's position). It returns at once; when the user chooses an item, its OnSelect runs on the UI thread, then done (if not nil) with chosen true; when the user dismisses the menu, done runs with chosen false.

```go
err := desktop.PopupMenu(w, tela.Point{X: e.X, Y: e.Y}, []desktop.MenuItem{
    {Label: "Copy", Accelerator: "Ctrl+C", OnSelect: copySelection},
    {Label: "Paste", Accelerator: "Ctrl+V", OnSelect: paste},
}, nil)
if errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
    setMenuOpen.Set(true) // draw the menu instead
}
```

The zero WindowHandle means the window the call comes from. The returned error says the menu could not be shown, and done is then never called: no running app, or no native context menus (errors.Is(err, [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables)): Linux, where Tela draws every menu). Call it on the UI thread. Tests answer the menu with telatest's App.ChoosePopupItem and App.DismissPopupMenu.

**Example**

A context menu: the OS's where there is one, else a drawn menu.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    drawnAt, setDrawnAt := tela.UseState[*tela.Point](nil)
    items := []desktop.MenuItem{
        {Label: "Copy", Accelerator: "Ctrl+C", OnSelect: func() {}},
        {Label: "Paste", Accelerator: "Ctrl+V", OnSelect: func() {}},
    }
    return Div(Class("h-full"),
        OnContextMenu(func(e tela.MouseEvent) {
            at := tela.Point{X: e.X, Y: e.Y}
            if err := desktop.PopupMenu(tela.WindowHandle{}, at, items, nil); errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
                setDrawnAt.Set(&at) // draw the menu at at
            }
        }),
        If(drawnAt != nil, Text("drawn menu")),
    )
})
```

### func ReadClipboard

```go
func ReadClipboard(done func(dt *tela.DataTransfer, err error), types ...string) error
```

ReadClipboard reads the clipboard and calls done, later, on the UI thread, with a DataTransfer holding what it read: the given types that the clipboard offers, or, with no types, the well-known ones it offers (text, HTML, a PNG image, files). Types are MIME types or HTML's names ("text", "Files", "url"). An empty clipboard gives an empty DataTransfer.

```go
desktop.ReadClipboard(func(dt *tela.DataTransfer, err error) {
    switch {
    case err != nil:
    case len(dt.Files()) > 0:
        attach(dt.Files())
    case dt.Has("image/png"):
        img, _ := dt.Image()
        insertImage(img)
    default:
        insertText(dt.Text())
    }
})
```

The DataTransfer is the caller's: it may keep and change it. Call it on the UI thread; done runs exactly once unless ReadClipboard returns an error (no running app, or [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) on a desktop whose clipboard has only text: use [`ReadClipboardText`](#func-readclipboardtext)). Tests preset the clipboard with telatest's App.SetClipboard.

**Example**

Copy rich text, and paste whatever the clipboard holds.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    pasted, setPasted := tela.UseState("")
    copyNote := func() {
        var dt tela.DataTransfer
        dt.SetHTML("<b>Groceries</b>: milk, eggs")
        dt.SetText("Groceries: milk, eggs")
        _ = desktop.WriteClipboard(&dt)
    }
    paste := func() {
        _ = desktop.ReadClipboard(func(dt *tela.DataTransfer, err error) {
            switch {
            case err != nil:
            case len(dt.Files()) > 0:
                setPasted.Set(fmt.Sprintf("%d files", len(dt.Files())))
            default:
                setPasted.Set(dt.Text())
            }
        })
    }
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(copyNote), Text("Copy")),
        Button(OnClick(paste), Text("Paste")),
        Text(pasted),
    )
})
```

### func ReadClipboardText

```go
func ReadClipboardText(done func(text string, err error)) error
```

ReadClipboardText reads the clipboard's text and calls done, later, on the UI thread ("" when it holds no text). It works on every desktop.

### func Register

```go
func Register(a Association, opts ...RegisterOption) (changed bool, err error)
```

Register makes the app a candidate handler of a URL scheme or a file type, for the current user (no administrator rights): the app appears in "Open with", and links of its scheme open it when no other application is the default. It does not make it the default ([`MakeDefault`](#func-makedefault)). It looks first, and writes nothing when the app is registered already (changed false). The app registers as an editor of a file type and a viewer of a scheme, unless [`Association.WithRole`](#func-association-withrole) gives another role; [`HandlerNone`](#type-handlerrole) declares a file type without opening it.

```go
if _, err := desktop.Register(desktop.URLScheme("notes")); err != nil {
    log.Print(err)
}
desktop.Register(desktop.FileType(".note", "application/x-notes-note", "Notes document"))
```

Linux writes the app's own .desktop file in \~/.local/share/applications (and a MIME type for a new extension); Windows writes HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Classes; macOS adds the scheme or the document type (and a type declaration for a new extension) to the app bundle's Info.plist and registers the bundle with Launch Services, so the program must be in a bundle (`tela build`, `tela run`; ErrUnsupported otherwise). Launch Services makes the only app that handles a scheme or a type its handler by itself. It works without a running app (an installer, a setup command), and is safe from any goroutine; it does file or registry I/O, so an app calls it from a goroutine or at start. The OS opens the app with the link or the files as arguments: read them with [`UseLaunch`](#func-uselaunch) (with [`SingleInstance`](#func-singleinstance), in the running app). While an app runs (telatest included), the calls go to its backend, which tests inspect with telatest's App.Registrations.

**Example**

Register notes: links and .note files for the user, and become their default handler only when asked.

```go
notes := desktop.URLScheme("notes")
doc := desktop.FileType(".note", "application/x-notes-note", "Notes document")
for _, a := range []desktop.Association{notes, doc} {
    if _, err := desktop.Register(a); err != nil {
        fmt.Println(err) // errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrAssociationTaken): ask before desktop.Replace()
    }
}
makeDefault := func() {
    r, err := desktop.MakeDefault(doc)
    if err == nil && r == desktop.DefaultAsked {
        fmt.Println("Choose Notes in the Default apps settings")
    }
}
_ = makeDefault
```

### func RegisterApp

```go
func RegisterApp(opts ...RegisterOption) (changed bool, err error)
```

RegisterApp makes the desktop know the app, without any URL scheme or file type (ADR-217). On Linux it writes the app's own desktop entry, \~/.local/share/applications/\<AppID\>.desktop, per user, with NoDisplay=true (no launcher in the menus) and no file types: the Linux global shortcuts portal refuses an app without one ([`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut)). Scheme and file-type registration ([`Register`](#func-register)) share that file. It looks first and writes nothing when the entry is up to date or another program's entry of the ID exists (a package's: never taken over without [`Replace`](#func-replace)). On Windows, which needs no entry, it writes nothing. On macOS the app bundle is the registration: RegisterApp registers it with Launch Services when Launch Services does not know it yet, and UnregisterApp writes nothing.

```go
func main() {
    desktop.SetAppID("com.example.notes")
    if _, err := desktop.RegisterApp(); err != nil {
        log.Print(err)
    }
    tela.Main(App)
}
```

Call it from the installed program, at start: the entry runs os.Executable ([`ForApp`](#func-forapp) gives another path, as an installer does). Under tela dev it returns ErrDevExecutable without Exec; under go run the program is a temporary build, so skip it there (on macOS it is not in a bundle either: ErrUnsupported, use `tela run`). It does file I/O and is safe from any goroutine; without a running app it uses the OS directly, and while an app runs (telatest included) its backend, which tests inspect with telatest's App.RegisteredApps.

### func SaveFile

```go
func SaveFile(done func(path string, err error), opts ...DialogOption) error
```

SaveFile shows the OS's save-file dialog and calls done with the chosen path ("" with a nil error: canceled). The OS asks before overwriting an existing file; done only gets the path, and the app writes the file. [`DefaultName`](#func-defaultname) suggests a name. Same rules as [`OpenFile`](#func-openfile).

```go
desktop.SaveFile(func(path string, err error) {
    if err == nil && path != "" {
        save(path)
    }
}, desktop.DefaultName("Untitled.md"), desktop.Filter("Markdown", "*.md"))
```

### func SavePlacement

```go
func SavePlacement(key string, p tela.WindowPlacement) error
```

SavePlacement saves p under key ([`UseSavePlacement`](#func-usesaveplacement) does it by itself). The zero placement deletes the saved one.

### func Secret

```go
func Secret(name string) ([]byte, error)
```

Secret returns the secret stored under name for this app, or an error wrapping [`ErrSecretNotFound`](#variables). It blocks; see [`SetSecret`](#func-setsecret).

```go
key, err := desktop.Secret("notes-key")
switch {
case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrSecretNotFound):
    key = newKey() // first run
case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported):
    disableLockedNotes()
}
```

**Example**

A key kept in the OS's keyring, read off the UI thread.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    status, setStatus := tela.UseState("unlocking…")
    tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
        key, err := desktop.Secret("notes-key")
        switch {
        case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrSecretNotFound):
            setStatus.Set("no key yet")
        case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrSecretCanceled):
            setStatus.Set("the keyring stayed locked")
        case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported):
            setStatus.Set("locked notes need a keyring")
        case err == nil:
            setStatus.Set(fmt.Sprintf("a %d-byte key", len(key)))
        }
    }, tela.Once)
    return Text(status)
})
```

### func SetAppID

```go
func SetAppID(id string)
```

SetAppID sets the name of the app's directories and settings ([`ConfigDir`](#func-configdir) and the others): use the reverse-DNS name given to tela.App.AppID ("com.example.notes"). Call it at the start of main, before anything reads a directory or a setting; [`PersistApp`](#func-persistapp) calls it with the App's AppID. Without it, the directories are named after the running app's App.AppID, or before tela.Run (and without an AppID) after the executable. Safe from any goroutine.

The same ID ([`AppID`](#func-appid)) is the one the desktop knows the app by: the name of its desktop entry ([`RegisterApp`](#func-registerapp)), which the Linux global shortcuts portal needs, and the app of its notifications. tela.Run gives it to the OS services when it starts, so a later SetAppID changes only the directories.

### func SetSecret

```go
func SetSecret(name string, secret []byte) error
```

SetSecret stores secret under name in the OS's secure storage, for this app ([`AppID`](#func-appid)), replacing an earlier value: the Credential Manager on Windows, the Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) on Linux. Use it for passwords, tokens and encryption keys, never in a plain file.

```go
tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
    if err := desktop.SetSecret("sync-token", token); err != nil {
        tela.Post(func() { setError.Set(err.Error()) })
    }
}, token)
```

The secret functions block: the OS may show a prompt to unlock the keyring and wait for the user. Call them from a goroutine (tela.UseGo), not from a handler or an effect, which would freeze the app; they are safe from any goroutine, and dev mode warns when one runs on the UI thread. A desktop without secure storage returns an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables); a canceled prompt [`ErrSecretCanceled`](#variables). They need a running app (tela.Run or telatest). Tests preset and read secrets with telatest's App.SetStoredSecret and App.StoredSecret.

### func ShowMessage

```go
func ShowMessage(m Message, done func(Answer)) error
```

ShowMessage shows a message box and calls done with the button the user chose (done may be nil). Closing the box without a button (Escape, its close button) answers [`Buttons.DismissAnswer`](#func-buttons-dismissanswer); Enter chooses [`Buttons.DefaultAnswer`](#func-buttons-defaultanswer).

```go
desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{
    Kind:    desktop.MessageQuestion,
    Title:   "Unsaved changes",
    Text:    "Save the changes to \"Groceries\" before closing?",
    Buttons: desktop.ButtonsYesNoCancel,
}, func(a desktop.Answer) {
    switch a {
    case desktop.AnswerYes:
        saveAndClose()
    case desktop.AnswerNo:
        closeWithoutSaving()
    } // AnswerCancel: keep editing
})
```

The box is the OS's where it has one (Windows); elsewhere (Linux, whose desktop portal has no message box) Tela draws it in a small modal window with the app's theme tokens, in light and dark. Call it on the UI thread (a handler, an effect; from a goroutine, wrap it in tela.Post). It returns at once and done runs later on the UI thread, exactly once. The error says no box could be shown (no running app, or no window to show a drawn box in); done is then never called. Tests answer it with telatest's App.AnswerMessage.

**Example**

A question before closing a document.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    win := tela.UseWindow()
    return Button(OnClick(func() {
        desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{
            Kind:    desktop.MessageQuestion,
            Title:   "Unsaved changes",
            Text:    "Save the changes before closing?",
            Buttons: desktop.ButtonsYesNoCancel,
        }, func(a desktop.Answer) {
            if a != desktop.AnswerCancel {
                win.Close()
            }
        })
    }), Text("Close"))
})
```

### func SingleInstance

```go
func SingleInstance(app tela.App) tela.App
```

SingleInstance returns app made a single-instance app: when the app is started while it already runs, the new process hands its launch (its arguments and working directory) to the running one and exits with status 0 before opening any window (tela.Run returns nil at once). The running app brings its main window to the front (showing it if it was hidden in the tray) and gives the launch to its [`UseLaunch`](#func-uselaunch) handlers:

```go
func main() {
    tela.Main(desktop.SingleInstance(desktop.PersistApp(tela.App{
        AppID: "com.example.Notes",
        Title: "Notes",
        Root:  Notes{},
    })))
}

func (n Notes) Build() tela.Node {
    desktop.UseLaunch(func(l desktop.Launch) {
        for _, p := range l.Files() { openNote(p) }
        for _, u := range l.URLs() { openLink(u) } // notes:open?id=3
    })
    // ...
}
```

Instances are told apart by the app ID ([`AppID`](#func-appid): [`SetAppID`](#func-setappid)'s, else app.AppID, else the executable's name), per user session: give the app an AppID. When the desktop cannot tell (no D-Bus session on Linux), the app runs on its own and a dev warning says why. Under tela dev the supervisor holds the claim across reloads (a second tela dev of the same app exits as a second instance). telatest claims nothing: App.InjectLaunch plays a second start.

**Example**

One window for every start of the app: a second start, from a file manager or a notes: link, opens its files and links in the running app.

```go
app := desktop.SingleInstance(tela.App{
    AppID: "com.example.Notes",
    Title: "Notes",
    Root: tela.C(func() tela.Node {
        open, setOpen := tela.UseState([]string(nil))
        desktop.UseLaunch(func(l desktop.Launch) {
            setOpen.Update(func(o []string) []string { return append(o, append(l.Files(), l.URLs()...)...) })
        })
        return Div(Map(open, func(p string) tela.Node { return Div(Key(p), Text(p)) }))
    }),
})
_ = app // tela.Main(app)
```

### func StateDir

```go
func StateDir() (string, error)
```

StateDir returns the app's folder for state worth keeping across runs but not worth backing up (window placements, recent files, history), creating it if needed:

- Linux: $XDG_STATE_HOME/\<app ID\> (\~/.local/state/\<app ID\>)
- Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\\\<app ID\>
- macOS: \~/Library/Application Support/\<app ID\>

### func Unregister

```go
func Unregister(a Association, opts ...RegisterOption) (changed bool, err error)
```

Unregister removes what Register and MakeDefault wrote for a: the app is no longer a candidate, and a default that names it is removed. Another application's entries are never touched. Nothing to remove is not an error (changed false).

### func UnregisterApp

```go
func UnregisterApp(opts ...RegisterOption) (changed bool, err error)
```

UnregisterApp removes the entry RegisterApp wrote, unless schemes or file types registered with [`Register`](#func-register) still need it: they keep it, and the [`Unregister`](#func-unregister) of the last one removes it. An entry Tela did not write is never touched. Nothing to remove is not an error.

### func UseLaunch

```go
func UseLaunch(f func(Launch))
```

UseLaunch calls f, on the UI thread, with each launch of the app: once with the process's own start, after the component mounts (LaunchStart), with every later start that [`SingleInstance`](#func-singleinstance) forwarded to this process (LaunchForwarded), and with the links and files the OS opens with the running app (LaunchOpened: macOS Launch Services, also the file that started the app, just after the start). Launches that arrive before the app's first frame wait for it, so the UseLaunch calls of the first frame get them. Use Launch.Files and Launch.URLs to open what the user asked for:

```go
desktop.UseLaunch(func(l desktop.Launch) {
    for _, p := range l.Files() {
        openNote(p)
    }
})
```

The process's own start is given to the UseLaunch calls mounted when the first of them mounts (normally the app's first frame), not to those that mount later, so a screen that mounts again does not reopen the files. telatest gives no start launch (App.InjectLaunch gives later ones), and neither does a reload of tela dev.

### func UseSavePlacement

```go
func UseSavePlacement(key string)
```

UseSavePlacement saves the placement of the window the calling component renders in (tela.UseWindow) under key: when it changes (the user moved, resized, maximized it; written half a second after the last change) and when the component unmounts (the window closes, the app quits). Read it back with [`LoadPlacement`](#func-loadplacement):

```go
tela.Window{
    Title:     "Inspector",
    Placement: desktop.LoadPlacement("inspector"),
    OnClose:   func() { setOpen.Set(false) },
    Root:      Inspector{}, // Inspector's Build calls desktop.UseSavePlacement("inspector")
}
```

[`SavedWindow`](#type-savedwindow) and [`PersistApp`](#func-persistapp) do both. key must stay the same for the life of the component. A tree without windows (tela snapshot) saves nothing.

### func UseSetting

```go
func UseSetting[T any](key string, def T) (T, tela.Setter[T])
```

UseSetting returns the value of key in the app's settings ([`Settings`](#func-settings)), or def when it has none, and a setter that stores a new value: the useState of a setting. The component builds again when the value changes, whoever changed it (this component, another one with the same key, Settings().Set from any goroutine, another program writing the file), and the store writes the file shortly after a change.

```go
func (Editor) Build() tela.Node {
    size, setSize := desktop.UseSetting("editor.fontSize", 14)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func() { setSize.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) }), Text("A+")),
        Textarea(Style(tela.FontSize(float32(size)))),
    )
}
```

T must encode as JSON. def is the value only while key has none: a stored value that does not decode into T (the setting changed type between versions of the app) reads as def too. A stored value replaces def, with one exception: a struct field the stored value does not have keeps def's, so a field added in a new version of the app has its default. Slices, arrays and maps the stored value has are replaced whole and their elements start empty, never from def's element at the same index: a field an element omits ("omitempty") is the zero value, not def's. def itself is never modified, and the value shares no memory with it. key must stay the same for the life of the component (give it another tela key to read another setting).

**Example**

A setting read and written by a component.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    dark, setDark := desktop.UseSetting("dark", false)
    return Button(OnClick(func() { setDark.Set(!dark) }), Textf("Dark mode: %v", dark))
})
```

### func UseStoreSetting

```go
func UseStoreSetting[T any](s *Store, key string, def T) (T, tela.Setter[T])
```

UseStoreSetting is [`UseSetting`](#func-usesetting) for a key of store s instead of the app's settings; the default and the stored value combine as UseSetting describes.

### func WriteClipboard

```go
func WriteClipboard(dt *tela.DataTransfer) error
```

WriteClipboard replaces the clipboard's content with dt's, every representation of it, so another application pastes the one it understands:

```go
var dt tela.DataTransfer
dt.SetHTML("<b>Groceries</b>: milk, eggs")
dt.SetText("Groceries: milk, eggs")
err := desktop.WriteClipboard(&dt)
```

A nil or empty dt empties the clipboard. Call it on the UI thread. It returns an error when no app runs, or wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) on a desktop whose clipboard takes only text (use [`WriteClipboardText`](#func-writeclipboardtext)).

### func WriteClipboardText

```go
func WriteClipboardText(text string) error
```

WriteClipboardText puts text on the clipboard, replacing its content. Call it on the UI thread.

## Types

### type Answer

```go
type Answer uint8
```

Answer is the button the user chose in a message box.

```go
const (
    AnswerOK Answer = iota
    AnswerCancel
    AnswerYes
    AnswerNo
)
```

#### func (Answer) String

```go
func (a Answer) String() string
```

### type AppMenuBar

```go
type AppMenuBar struct {
    // Menus are the bar's top-level entries ("File", "Edit"), each with
    // its Submenu. A menu role (RoleEditMenu, RoleWindowMenu) with no
    // Submenu gets the standard items.
    Menus []MenuItem
    // AppItems are the items of macOS's app menu after About and before
    // Services ("Settings…"), separated from them by macOS. Ignored where
    // there is no app menu. Menu roles are not allowed among them.
    AppItems []MenuItem
    // OnError receives the error when the bar cannot be shown or updated
    // (ErrUnsupported where there is no menu bar to give). Nil reports it
    // as a dev warning.
    OnError func(err error)
    // NativeOnly gives the bar only where the platform has an app menu
    // bar (macOS): elsewhere it is not put in the windows' menu bars
    // (Windows), and OnError receives an error wrapping ErrUnsupported
    // (nil OnError: no dev warning, the app asked for nothing else). An app
    // that draws its own title bar or menus on Windows and Linux declares
    // its macOS menu bar this way, unconditionally.
    NativeOnly bool
}
```

AppMenuBar is a component that gives the app its menu bar while it is mounted, declared once anywhere in the tree (ADR-224; Electron's Menu.setApplicationMenu), follows its fields, and restores the default when it unmounts. It renders nothing where it is declared.

```go
desktop.AppMenuBar{
    AppItems: []desktop.MenuItem{
        {Label: "Settings…", Accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+,", OnSelect: openSettings},
    },
    Menus: []desktop.MenuItem{
        {Label: "File", Submenu: []desktop.MenuItem{
            {Label: "New Note", Accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+N", OnSelect: newNote},
            {Separator: true},
            {Role: desktop.RoleClose},
        }},
        {Role: desktop.RoleEditMenu},
        {Role: desktop.RoleWindowMenu},
    },
    OnError: func(err error) { setDrawnMenu.Set(true) },
}
```

Where the platform has an app menu bar (macOS), it is the menu bar of every window, and macOS always puts the app's own menu first (About, then AppItems such as Settings…, then Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All and Quit). On Windows, where each framed window has a menu bar, it becomes the bar of every framed window that has no [`MenuBar`](#type-menubar) of its own, including windows that open later; a window's own MenuBar wins on that window. AppItems are ignored there. Elsewhere (Linux; frameless and TitleBarOverlay windows; a tree with no window of a running app, as in tela snapshot; with NativeOnly, everywhere but the platform's app menu bar) OnError receives an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) after the first build, and the app draws its menu instead (kit's Menubar with AppMenu does). Nil OnError reports it as a dev warning. Two mounted AppMenuBars: the later one wins, with a dev warning.

Choosing an item runs its OnSelect on the UI thread. Role items ([`Role`](#type-role)) without an OnSelect are carried out by the OS where it can (macOS) and by package desktop elsewhere, on the window with the keyboard focus.

On macOS an Accelerator is the item's key equivalent: the key chooses the item and does not reach the app as a key event, so do not handle the key a second time (no h.OnKeyDown for it). "CmdOrCtrl+N" is the portable spelling: Command+N on a Mac, Ctrl+N elsewhere, where the accelerator is display text and the app handles the key itself. Tests read the bar with telatest's App.AppMenuBar and choose items with App.ChooseAppMenuItem.

#### func (AppMenuBar) Build

```go
func (m AppMenuBar) Build() tela.Node
```

Build sets the app's menu bar while the component is mounted.

### type AppRegistration

```go
type AppRegistration struct {
    // Registered: the desktop knows the app's ID (on Linux an entry
    // <ID>.desktop exists, whoever wrote it; always on Windows, which
    // needs none; on macOS Launch Services knows a bundle of the ID).
    Registered bool
    // Requested: RegisterApp wrote the entry, and UnregisterApp would
    // remove it.
    Requested bool
    // Other is the path of an entry of the app's ID that Tela did not
    // write (a package's, an installer's), "" when there is none.
    Other string
}
```

AppRegistration is what [`AppStatus`](#func-appstatus) reports.

#### func AppStatus

```go
func AppStatus(opts ...RegisterOption) (AppRegistration, error)
```

AppStatus reports whether the desktop knows the app, and whether RegisterApp wrote its entry.

### type Association

```go
type Association struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Association is a URL scheme or a file type the app opens: build it with [`URLScheme`](#func-urlscheme) or [`FileType`](#func-filetype).

#### func FileType

```go
func FileType(extension, mimeType, description string) Association
```

FileType returns the association of a file extension, given with its dot (".note"), with its MIME type ("application/x-notes-note") and a description of the type in the user's language ("Notes document"), all required: Linux associates apps with MIME types, and registers this one for the extension when no other type claims it.

#### func URLScheme

```go
func URLScheme(name string) Association
```

URLScheme returns the association of a URL scheme of the app's own, given without ':' ("notes" for notes:open?id=3 links): a letter, then letters, digits, '+', '-' or '.'. Standard schemes (http, mailto…) belong to other applications and panic.

#### func (Association) Role

```go
func (a Association) Role() HandlerRole
```

Role returns a's role: HandlerDefault unless WithRole set another.

#### func (Association) String

```go
func (a Association) String() string
```

String returns "notes:" for a scheme, ".note" for a file type.

#### func (Association) WithRole

```go
func (a Association) WithRole(r HandlerRole) Association
```

WithRole returns a copy of a with the role r. macOS writes it in the bundle's Info.plist (CFBundleTypeRole; HandlerNone also with LSHandlerRank None). Linux and Windows have no roles, so Editor, Viewer and Shell register the same handler there; HandlerNone registers the type's MIME package on Linux and its ProgID (description, icon) on Windows, without the entries that open files with the app.

```go
// Notes edits .note files, opens .notes-backup ones read-only, and
// only gives .notes-index files (which it writes) a name and an icon.
desktop.Register(desktop.FileType(".note", "application/x-notes-note", "Notes document"))
desktop.Register(desktop.FileType(".notes-backup", "application/x-notes-backup", "Notes backup").
    WithRole(desktop.HandlerViewer))
desktop.Register(desktop.FileType(".notes-index", "application/x-notes-index", "Notes index").
    WithRole(desktop.HandlerNone))
```

The role is not part of what a registration is: Register with another role changes the registration that is there (changed true), and Unregister and RegistrationStatus address the scheme or extension whatever the role. RegistrationStatus with HandlerNone reports whether the type is declared; with another role, whether the app opens it.

### type Buttons

```go
type Buttons uint8
```

Buttons is the set of buttons of a message box: the sets every native message box has.

```go
const (
    ButtonsOK          Buttons = iota // OK (the default)
    ButtonsOKCancel                   // OK and Cancel
    ButtonsYesNo                      // Yes and No
    ButtonsYesNoCancel                // Yes, No and Cancel
)
```

#### func (Buttons) DefaultAnswer

```go
func (b Buttons) DefaultAnswer() Answer
```

DefaultAnswer is the button Enter chooses: OK, or Yes for the sets with Yes.

#### func (Buttons) DismissAnswer

```go
func (b Buttons) DismissAnswer() Answer
```

DismissAnswer is the answer of a box with buttons b that the user closes without a button (Escape, the close button): Cancel when the set has it, OK for ButtonsOK and No for ButtonsYesNo.

#### func (Buttons) Has

```go
func (b Buttons) Has(a Answer) bool
```

Has reports whether the set b has the button a.

### type DefaultResult

```go
type DefaultResult uint8
```

DefaultResult is what [`MakeDefault`](#func-makedefault) did.

```go
const (
    // DefaultNone: nothing was done; MakeDefault returns it with every
    // error (the zero value: a failure never reads as DefaultSet).
    DefaultNone DefaultResult = iota
    // DefaultSet: the app is now the default handler.
    DefaultSet
    // DefaultAsked: the OS lets only the user choose (Windows file
    // types), so the system's Default apps settings opened; tell the user
    // to pick the app there, and check later with RegistrationStatus.
    DefaultAsked
)
```

#### func MakeDefault

```go
func MakeDefault(a Association, opts ...RegisterOption) (DefaultResult, error)
```

MakeDefault asks for the app to become the default handler of a, registering it first if needed (with Register's rules and options). Where the OS lets an app set it (Linux; Windows schemes; macOS, through Launch Services, without a prompt) it is set at once (DefaultSet). For Windows file types only the user can choose: MakeDefault opens the system's Default apps settings and returns DefaultAsked. On an error it returns DefaultNone. Call it only when the user asked ("Make Notes the default app for .note files").

#### func (DefaultResult) String

```go
func (r DefaultResult) String() string
```

### type DialogOption

```go
type DialogOption struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

DialogOption configures a file dialog: [`Title`](#func-title), [`Directory`](#func-directory), [`DefaultName`](#func-defaultname), [`Filter`](#func-filter) and [`Parent`](#func-parent).

#### func DefaultName

```go
func DefaultName(name string) DialogOption
```

DefaultName suggests the file name of a [`SaveFile`](#func-savefile) dialog ("Untitled.md"). The other dialogs ignore it.

#### func Directory

```go
func Directory(dir string) DialogOption
```

Directory sets the folder the dialog starts in (default: the OS's choice, usually the folder used last).

#### func Filter

```go
func Filter(name string, patterns ...string) DialogOption
```

Filter adds an entry to the dialog's list of file types: a label and glob patterns ("\*.png"). Repeat it for several entries; the first is selected. Without filters the dialog shows every file. [`PickFolder`](#func-pickfolder) ignores it.

```go
desktop.OpenFile(done,
    desktop.Filter("Images", "*.png", "*.jpg", "*.webp"),
    desktop.Filter("All files", "*"))
```

#### func Filters

```go
func Filters(filters ...FileFilter) DialogOption
```

Filters adds several entries at once, as [`Filter`](#func-filter) does for one.

#### func Parent

```go
func Parent(w tela.WindowHandle) DialogOption
```

Parent makes the dialog modal to w's window (tela.UseWindow). The default is the window the call comes from: the window whose handler or effect is running, else the focused window, else the main window.

#### func Title

```go
func Title(title string) DialogOption
```

Title sets the dialog's title (default: the OS's, such as "Open").

### type FileFilter

```go
type FileFilter struct {
    // Name is the label shown for the entry ("Images").
    Name string
    // Patterns are glob patterns of file names: "*.png", "*.jpg", "*".
    Patterns []string
}
```

FileFilter is one entry of a file dialog's list of types: a label and the glob patterns of the file names it shows.

### type GlobalShortcut

```go
type GlobalShortcut struct {
    // ID identifies the shortcut to the OS, which keeps the user's
    // changes to it across runs (the portal): keep it stable
    // ("new-note"). Required; unique among the mounted shortcuts. When two
    // mounted components share an ID (a dev warning), the one that
    // registered last owns it and gets its events; the other stays
    // displaced, even after the owner unmounts, until its own ID, Keys or
    // Description change, when it registers again and becomes the owner.
    ID string
    // Keys is the preferred key combination, such as "Ctrl+Alt+N" or
    // "Super+F5" (see [ParseKeys] for the names). Required; a combination
    // that cannot be parsed panics in dev mode and is reported to
    // OnStatus as ShortcutFailed otherwise (keys a user typed: check them
    // with ParseKeys first).
    Keys string
    // Description says what the shortcut does, in the user's language
    // ("Create a note"); the desktop's shortcut settings show it.
    // Required.
    Description string
    // OnPress runs when the user presses the shortcut.
    OnPress func()
    // OnRelease runs when the user releases it, where the OS reports
    // releases (Linux; not Windows).
    OnRelease func()
    // OnStatus receives the outcome of the registration and its later
    // changes (the user bound other keys, or removed the shortcut). Nil
    // reports a status other than ShortcutBound as a dev warning.
    OnStatus func(ShortcutStatusEvent)
}
```

GlobalShortcut is a component that registers a system-wide keyboard shortcut while it is mounted: OnPress runs, on the UI thread, when the user presses Keys anywhere, even while another application has the focus. It follows its fields (registering again only when ID, Keys or Description change) and unregisters when it unmounts. It renders nothing where it is declared; several, with different IDs, may be mounted at once.

```go
desktop.GlobalShortcut{
    ID:          "new-note",
    Keys:        "Ctrl+Alt+N",
    Description: "Create a note",
    OnPress:     func() { win.Show(); newNote() },
    OnStatus: func(e desktop.ShortcutStatusEvent) {
        if e.Status != desktop.ShortcutBound {
            setHint.Set(e.Err.Error()) // "Ctrl+Alt+N is taken by another application"
        }
    },
}
```

The OS decides: Windows refuses a combination another application holds (ShortcutTaken), and on Wayland the desktop asks the user first (through the GlobalShortcuts portal) and may bind other keys, which ShortcutStatusEvent.Trigger reports, or none (Hyprland: see ShortcutStatusEvent.Trigger). Where the desktop has no global shortcuts (Wayland without the portal), OnStatus receives ShortcutFailed with an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables). Tests press it with telatest's App.PressShortcut.

On Linux the portal needs the app's desktop entry: call [`RegisterApp`](#func-registerapp) once in the installed program (at start, before tela.Run), or the shortcut fails with an error wrapping [`ErrAppNotRegistered`](#variables) that names the entry. Give the app an ID ([`SetAppID`](#func-setappid) or tela.App.AppID): the executable's name is the default.

**Example**

A shortcut that works from any application, and a hint when the OS would not bind it.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    win := tela.UseWindow()
    hint, setHint := tela.UseState("")
    return Div(
        desktop.GlobalShortcut{
            ID:          "new-note",
            Keys:        "Ctrl+Alt+N",
            Description: "Create a note",
            OnPress:     func() { win.Show() },
            OnStatus: func(e desktop.ShortcutStatusEvent) {
                if e.Status == desktop.ShortcutBound {
                    setHint.Set("Press " + e.Trigger + " anywhere for a new note")
                } else {
                    setHint.Set(e.Err.Error())
                }
            },
        },
        Text(hint),
    )
})
```

#### func (GlobalShortcut) Build

```go
func (g GlobalShortcut) Build() tela.Node
```

Build registers the shortcut while the component is mounted (see [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut)).

### type HandlerApp

```go
type HandlerApp struct {
    // ID is the app ID, which names the app's registration (its .desktop
    // file on Linux, its ProgIDs on Windows; on macOS it must be the
    // bundle's CFBundleIdentifier, which `tela build` takes from
    // App.AppID). Default: [AppID].
    ID string
    // Name is shown in the desktop's "Open with" lists. Default: the
    // last part of the ID, capitalized ("com.example.notes" is "Notes").
    Name string
    // Exec is the absolute path of the program to run, with Args and then
    // the link or the files. Default: os.Executable. Under tela dev the
    // executable is a temporary dev build, so Register and MakeDefault
    // there need Exec given (ErrDevExecutable otherwise); under go run it
    // is a temporary build too: register from the installed program, or
    // give its path. On macOS it must be the program inside an app bundle
    // (<Name>.app/Contents/MacOS/), as `tela build` and `tela run` make
    // it: the registration is written in the bundle's Info.plist, and
    // every call outside a bundle returns an error wrapping
    // [ErrUnsupported].
    Exec string
    // Args are arguments put before the link or the files. Unused on
    // macOS, where the link or the files reach the app as a launch, not
    // as arguments.
    Args []string
    // Icon is the absolute path of the app's icon (PNG or SVG on Linux,
    // .ico on Windows; macOS shows the bundle's own icon). Optional.
    Icon string
}
```

HandlerApp describes the application registered as a handler: what the OS runs to open a link or a file. Its zero fields are the running program's (see [`RegisterOption`](#type-registeroption) ForApp).

### type HandlerRole

```go
type HandlerRole uint8
```

HandlerRole is what the app does with the files of a type, or the links of a scheme, it registers for ([`Association.WithRole`](#func-association-withrole)): the role of macOS's CFBundleTypeRole, Tauri's and electron-builder's file associations.

```go
const (
    // HandlerDefault (the zero value) is HandlerEditor for a file type and
    // HandlerViewer for a scheme.
    HandlerDefault HandlerRole = iota
    // HandlerEditor: the app opens, edits and saves files of the type.
    HandlerEditor
    // HandlerViewer: the app opens files of the type, or links of the
    // scheme, without editing them.
    HandlerViewer
    // HandlerShell: the app provides runtime services for the type
    // (macOS's Shell role; elsewhere the same as HandlerEditor).
    HandlerShell
    // HandlerNone: the app declares the file type, so the desktop knows
    // its name and icon (and, on Linux, detects its files), without
    // opening it: no "Open with" entry, never the default. For file types
    // only; a scheme with it panics, and so does MakeDefault.
    HandlerNone
)
```

#### func (HandlerRole) String

```go
func (r HandlerRole) String() string
```

### type Launch

```go
type Launch struct {
    // Args are the command-line arguments after the program's name, or
    // the links and files opened (files as paths).
    Args []string
    // Dir is the working directory of the process that was started, for
    // relative paths in Args.
    Dir string
    // Source says where the launch comes from: this process's own start,
    // another process of the app, or the OS.
    Source LaunchSource
    // AtStart reports a launch that came with this process's start: the
    // LaunchStart one, and on macOS the LaunchOpened that names the files
    // or links the user opened to start the app (Launch Services hands
    // them just after the start, ADR-259). An app that restores its last
    // session at start can skip it when such a launch names what to open.
    // Linux and Windows cannot tell (their LaunchOpened and
    // LaunchForwarded launches are false).
    AtStart bool
}
```

Launch is a request to open something: the command-line arguments and the working directory of a process of the app, or the links and files the OS opened with it. [`UseLaunch`](#func-uselaunch) gives the app its own start's, with [`SingleInstance`](#func-singleinstance) those of every later start that another process forwarded (a file opened from a file manager, a deep link such as "notes:open?id=3" clicked in a browser), and on macOS the links and files Launch Services hands the app. Source says which.

**Example**

The files a launch names, made absolute.

```go
l := desktop.Launch{Dir: "/home/ana", Args: []string{"--new-window", "notes:open?id=3", "file:///tmp/a%20b.note", "lists/groceries.note"}}
fmt.Println(l.URLs())
fmt.Println(l.Files())
// Output:
// [notes:open?id=3]
// [/tmp/a b.note /home/ana/lists/groceries.note]
```

#### func (Launch) Files

```go
func (l Launch) Files() []string
```

Files returns the arguments that are files or folders, as absolute paths, in order: relative paths are made absolute against Dir, and file: URIs (which Linux launchers pass for a .desktop file's %U) are turned into paths. The files may not exist. Flags and URLs are left out (see URLs).

#### func (Launch) URLs

```go
func (l Launch) URLs() []string
```

URLs returns the arguments that are URLs, in order: any "scheme:…" with a scheme of at least two characters ("notes:open?id=3", "<https://example.com>"), except file: URIs, which are files. Arguments that start with '-' are flags, neither URLs nor files (after a "--", every argument counts).

### type LaunchSource

```go
type LaunchSource uint8
```

LaunchSource says where a [`Launch`](#type-launch) comes from.

```go
const (
    // LaunchStart is this process's own start: its command line.
    LaunchStart LaunchSource = iota
    // LaunchForwarded is another process of the app, started while this
    // one runs, which [SingleInstance] forwarded to this one before it
    // exited: its command line.
    LaunchForwarded
    // LaunchOpened is the OS handing the running app links or files to
    // open, without another process of the app (Electron's open-url and
    // open-file events): on macOS a link clicked in another app or a file
    // opened from the Finder, the Dock or Open With, including the one
    // that started the app, which arrives just after the start (whose Args
    // are then empty); on Linux the desktop's launchers that call the
    // running instance over D-Bus (org.freedesktop.Application).
    LaunchOpened
)
```

#### func (LaunchSource) String

```go
func (s LaunchSource) String() string
```

### type MenuBar

```go
type MenuBar struct {
    // Menus are the bar's top-level entries ("File", "Edit"), each with
    // its Submenu.
    Menus []MenuItem
    // OnError receives the error when the bar cannot be shown or
    // updated (ErrUnsupported where windows have no native menu bar).
    // Nil reports it as a dev warning.
    OnError func(err error)
}
```

MenuBar is a component that gives the window it is in the OS's menu bar while it is mounted (a Windows window with a title bar), follows its fields, and removes the bar when it unmounts. Menus are the top-level entries, each with its Submenu; choosing an item runs its OnSelect on the UI thread. It renders nothing where it is declared.

```go
desktop.MenuBar{
    Menus: []desktop.MenuItem{
        {Label: "File", Submenu: []desktop.MenuItem{
            {Label: "New", Accelerator: "Ctrl+N", OnSelect: newNote},
            {Separator: true},
            {Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
        }},
    },
    OnError: func(err error) { setDrawnMenu.Set(true) },
}
```

Most desktops have no native window menu bars (Linux; frameless windows, which draw their own title bar; macOS, whose menu bar belongs to the app: a window's own bar is unsupported there, ADR-224, use [`AppMenuBar`](#type-appmenubar)), and where there is no window of a running app (tela snapshot): there OnError receives an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) after the first build, and the app draws its menu instead (kit's Menubar does). Accelerator texts are only shown: handle the keys yourself. A window's own MenuBar wins over the app's [`AppMenuBar`](#type-appmenubar) on that window. Tests choose items with telatest's App.ChooseMenuItem.

**Example**

A native menu bar, with a drawn one where windows have none.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    drawn, setDrawn := tela.UseState(false)
    menus := []desktop.MenuItem{
        {Label: "File", Submenu: []desktop.MenuItem{
            {Label: "New", Accelerator: "Ctrl+N", OnSelect: func() {}},
            {Separator: true},
            {Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
        }},
    }
    return Div(
        desktop.MenuBar{Menus: menus, OnError: func(error) { setDrawn.Set(true) }},
        If(drawn, Text("a drawn menu bar")),
    )
})
```

#### func (MenuBar) Build

```go
func (m MenuBar) Build() tela.Node
```

Build sets the menu bar while the component is mounted (see [`MenuBar`](#type-menubar)).

### type MenuItem

```go
type MenuItem struct {
    // Label is the item's text (plain text: "&" and "_" are shown as
    // they are).
    Label string
    // AccessKey is the item's access key in Windows menus (HTML's
    // accesskey; ADR-259): a letter or a digit, marked in the label where
    // it has that character ("F&ormat" for 'o'), else appended as the
    // native apps of Chinese, Japanese and Korean do ("ファイル(&F)"), so
    // a translated menu keeps the English keys. Zero, the usual value, lets
    // Windows menu bars choose one (the first free letter of the label, or
    // the role's English letter; tray and popup menus then have none).
    // Other platforms ignore it (macOS menus have no access keys; Tela's
    // drawn menus use typeahead).
    AccessKey rune
    // Accelerator is the text of the item's keyboard shortcut, shown at
    // its right ("Ctrl+S"; [ParseKeys] writes it the usual way). It is
    // display only: the app handles the key itself (h.OnKeyDown). Tray
    // menus may not show it. "CmdOrCtrl+N" is the portable spelling
    // (Command on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere). One exception: in the app's menu
    // bar on macOS ([AppMenuBar]) it is the item's key equivalent, so the
    // key chooses the item and does not reach the app as a key event: do
    // not handle it a second time.
    Accelerator string
    // Role makes the item, or its submenu, a standard one: Undo, Copy,
    // Minimize, the Edit menu (see [Role]). An empty Label gets the
    // role's. RoleNone, the zero value, is an item of the app's own.
    Role Role
    // Separator makes the item a separator line; the other fields are
    // ignored.
    Separator bool
    // Checkbox makes the item a check item, showing a check mark when
    // Checked.
    Checkbox, Checked bool
    // Disabled shows the item grayed out; it cannot be chosen.
    Disabled bool
    // Submenu, if not empty, makes the item open a submenu (OnSelect is
    // then never called).
    Submenu []MenuItem
    // OnSelect runs when the user chooses the item.
    OnSelect func()
}
```

MenuItem is an item of a native menu: a tray icon's ([`Tray`](#type-tray)), a window's menu bar ([`MenuBar`](#type-menubar)) or a context menu ([`PopupMenu`](#func-popupmenu)). The backend never toggles a checkbox: OnSelect updates the state that renders Checked.

```go
}
```
