### type RegisterOption

```go
type RegisterOption struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RegisterOption configures [`Register`](#func-register), [`Unregister`](#func-unregister), [`MakeDefault`](#func-makedefault), [`RegistrationStatus`](#func-registrationstatus), [`RegisterApp`](#func-registerapp), [`UnregisterApp`](#func-unregisterapp) and [`AppStatus`](#func-appstatus): [`Replace`](#func-replace) and [`ForApp`](#func-forapp).

#### func ForApp

```go
func ForApp(app HandlerApp) RegisterOption
```

ForApp sets what is registered instead of the running program: an installer registers the program it installed. Fields left empty keep their defaults (see [`HandlerApp`](#type-handlerapp)).

```go
desktop.Register(desktop.URLScheme("notes"), desktop.ForApp(desktop.HandlerApp{
    ID:   "com.example.Notes",
    Name: "Notes",
    Exec: `C:\Program Files\Notes\notes.exe`,
    Icon: `C:\Program Files\Notes\notes.ico`,
}))
```

#### func Replace

```go
func Replace() RegisterOption
```

Replace lets [`Register`](#func-register) (and MakeDefault, which registers first) take over an association another application holds: a Windows scheme key whose command runs another program, a Linux desktop entry of the app's ID that Tela did not write, an extension another MIME type claims. Without it Register returns an error wrapping [`ErrAssociationTaken`](#variables) and writes nothing. Ask the user before passing it.

### type Registration

```go
type Registration struct {
    // Registered: the app is a candidate handler (offered in "Open with",
    // or for the scheme), in any role but HandlerNone. Asked about an
    // Association with HandlerNone, it reports whether the file type is
    // declared (on Linux its MIME type is known, whoever installed it; on
    // Windows the app's ProgID exists; on macOS the Info.plist declares it
    // and Launch Services knows the bundle).
    Registered bool
    // Default: the app is the default handler; always false asked with
    // HandlerNone.
    Default bool
    // Other names what holds the association instead of the app (the
    // default handler, the owner of a Windows scheme key, the MIME type
    // that claims an extension on Linux, the default app's bundle ID on
    // macOS); "" when nothing does.
    Other string
    // Role is the role the app is registered with, whatever the role of
    // the Association asked about (ADR-259): HandlerNone for a file type
    // the app only declares; on macOS the role of the Info.plist entry
    // (an entry the developer wrote in the bundle keeps its own role,
    // which Register does not change); on Linux and Windows, which keep no
    // roles, HandlerDefault for a handler. HandlerDefault too when the app
    // is not registered.
    Role HandlerRole
}
```

Registration is what [`RegistrationStatus`](#func-registrationstatus) reports.

#### func RegistrationStatus

```go
func RegistrationStatus(a Association, opts ...RegisterOption) (Registration, error)
```

RegistrationStatus reports whether the app is registered for a, whether it is the default, and what else holds a.

### type Role

```go
type Role uint8
```

Role marks a [`MenuItem`](#type-menuitem) as a standard item or menu (ADR-226), with Electron's names: the edit actions, the window actions, and the Edit, Window and Help menus. The zero value, RoleNone, is an item of the app's own.

```go
desktop.MenuItem{Role: desktop.RoleCopy}       // "Copy", acting on the focused field
desktop.MenuItem{Role: desktop.RoleEditMenu}   // "Edit": Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All
desktop.MenuItem{Role: desktop.RoleMinimize, Label: "Minimizar"}
```

An item with a Role and no Label gets the role's label ([`Role.Label`](#func-role-label), English unless the app's catalogs translate it); a menu role with no Submenu gets the standard items, as Electron's role: 'editMenu' and 'windowMenu' do (RoleHelpMenu has no standard items: give it a Submenu).

What choosing a role item does depends on the platform. Where the OS has the action, it carries it out itself and the choice never reaches the app (macOS's app menu bar: AppKit's own items, acting on the key window and its focused field). Everywhere else package desktop carries it out: minimize, zoom (maximize or restore) and close act on the window the menu belongs to (the key window for the app's menu bar and the tray's menu), and the edit roles send that window's focused element the shortcut of its platform (Ctrl+C, or Command+C under the Mac key flavor), so text fields cut, copy, paste, undo and select all as they do for the keys. An item's own OnSelect, if set, runs instead, and the platform does not perform the role.

```go
const (
    // RoleNone is an item of the app's own.
    RoleNone Role = iota
    // RoleUndo and RoleRedo undo and redo the last edit of the focused
    // field.
    RoleUndo
    RoleRedo
    // RoleCut, RoleCopy, RolePaste and RoleSelectAll act on the focused
    // field.
    RoleCut
    RoleCopy
    RolePaste
    RoleSelectAll
    // RoleMinimize minimizes the window, RoleZoom maximizes it or restores
    // it, and RoleClose asks to close it as its close button does.
    RoleMinimize
    RoleZoom
    RoleClose
    // RoleEditMenu is the Edit menu (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select
    // All unless the item has a Submenu of its own).
    RoleEditMenu
    // RoleWindowMenu is the Window menu (Minimize, Zoom, Close unless the
    // item has a Submenu of its own): macOS lists the open windows at its
    // end.
    RoleWindowMenu
    // RoleHelpMenu is the Help menu: macOS adds its search field to it.
    // It needs a Submenu.
    RoleHelpMenu
)
```

#### func (Role) Label

```go
func (r Role) Label() string
```

Label returns the role's default label: "Undo", "Select All", "Edit"... in the app's language ("" for RoleNone). It is the built-in label of the role (ADR-251: "tela.menu.undo", "tela.menu.selectAll"... of [`tela.Labels`](API-Reference-tela#func-labels)), English unless the app's catalogs translate it.

#### func (Role) String

```go
func (r Role) String() string
```

String returns Electron's name of the role: "undo", "selectAll", "editMenu"... ("" for RoleNone).

### type SavedWindow

```go
type SavedWindow struct {
    // Key names the window's saved placement; required and unique in the
    // app ("main" is PersistApp's).
    Key string
    // Window is the window to open.
    Window tela.Window
}
```

SavedWindow is a tela.Window that opens where the user left it: the placement saved under Key is its Placement (unless Window.Placement is set), and its placement is saved under Key when it changes and when it closes ([`UseSavePlacement`](#func-usesaveplacement)).

```go
If(inspectorOpen, tela.Component(desktop.SavedWindow{
    Key: "inspector",
    Window: tela.Window{
        Title: "Inspector", Width: 360, Height: 600,
        OnClose: func() { setInspectorOpen.Set(false) },
        Root:    Inspector{},
    },
}))
```

**Example**

A tool window that remembers where it was.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    open, setOpen := tela.UseState(false)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func() { setOpen.Set(true) }), Text("Inspector")),
        If(open, tela.Component(desktop.SavedWindow{
            Key: "inspector",
            Window: tela.Window{
                Title: "Inspector", Width: 360, Height: 600,
                OnClose: func() { setOpen.Set(false) },
                Root:    tela.C(func() tela.Node { return Text("Properties") }),
            },
        })),
    )
})
```

#### func (SavedWindow) Build

```go
func (s SavedWindow) Build() tela.Node
```

Build opens the window (see [`SavedWindow`](#type-savedwindow)).

### type ShortcutStatus

```go
type ShortcutStatus uint8
```

ShortcutStatus is the state of a [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut)'s registration.

```go
const (
    // ShortcutBound: the shortcut works; Trigger is what the user presses.
    ShortcutBound ShortcutStatus = iota
    // ShortcutTaken: another application holds the combination.
    ShortcutTaken
    // ShortcutRefused: the user or the desktop declined to bind it.
    ShortcutRefused
    // ShortcutRevoked: the user or the desktop removed it after it was
    // bound.
    ShortcutRevoked
    // ShortcutFailed: it could not be registered (no global shortcuts on
    // this desktop: ErrUnsupported; invalid Keys; an OS error).
    ShortcutFailed
)
```

#### func (ShortcutStatus) String

```go
func (s ShortcutStatus) String() string
```

### type ShortcutStatusEvent

```go
type ShortcutStatusEvent struct {
    // ID is the shortcut's.
    ID string
    // Status is the registration's state.
    Status ShortcutStatus
    // Trigger is the combination the user presses, as the desktop shows
    // it ("Ctrl+Alt+N"), for ShortcutBound: the desktop may bind other
    // keys than Keys. "" when it does not say, or has assigned no keys
    // yet: Hyprland registers the shortcut but ignores Keys, and the user
    // binds it in hyprland.conf with
    // "bind = CTRL ALT, N, global, <AppID>:<ID>"; it fires from then on.
    // Show the keys asked for, and say so.
    Trigger string
    // Err says why, for every status but ShortcutBound, in a sentence an
    // app can show ("desktop: the global shortcut Ctrl+Alt+N is taken by
    // another application").
    Err error
}
```

ShortcutStatusEvent is what [`GlobalShortcut`](#type-globalshortcut)'s OnStatus receives.

### type ShownNotification

```go
type ShownNotification struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ShownNotification is a notification on screen, returned by [`Notify`](#func-notify). The zero value is no notification.

#### func Notify

```go
func Notify(n Notification) (ShownNotification, error)
```

Notify shows a desktop notification. Its callbacks run on the UI thread, so they may set state; clicking the notification usually brings the app forward:

```go
win := tela.UseWindow()
...
desktop.Notify(desktop.Notification{
    Title:   "Export finished",
    Body:    "notes.pdf was saved in Documents.",
    OnClick: func() { win.Show() },
    Actions: []desktop.NotificationAction{
        {Label: "Open", OnClick: func() { tela.OpenPath(pdf) }},
    },
})
```

Call it on the UI thread (a handler, an effect; from a goroutine, wrap it in tela.Post). The error says the notification could not be shown: no running app, or no notification service (errors.Is(err, [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables))), where the app should show the news itself. Tests read the notifications with telatest's App.Notifications and click them with App.ClickNotification.

**Example**

A notification that brings the app back when clicked.

```go
_ = tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    win := tela.UseWindow()
    return Button(OnClick(func() {
        _, err := desktop.Notify(desktop.Notification{
            Title:   "Export finished",
            Body:    "notes.pdf was saved in Documents.",
            OnClick: func() { win.Show() },
        })
        if err != nil {
            fmt.Println("no notifications:", err)
        }
    }), Text("Export"))
})
```

#### func (ShownNotification) Close

```go
func (n ShownNotification) Close() error
```

Close withdraws the notification; its callbacks are not called any more. Closing one that is gone does nothing. UI thread.

#### func (ShownNotification) IsZero

```go
func (n ShownNotification) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether n is the zero ShownNotification.

### type Store

```go
type Store struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Store is a small key-value store kept in a JSON file: an app's settings ([`Settings`](#func-settings)) or any other small state. Values are anything encoding/json encodes; reads decode them into the caller's type. Writes are kept in memory and written to the file shortly after (coalesced: a slider that sets a value every frame writes a few times a second), atomically (a temporary file renamed over the old one, so a crash never leaves half a file), and when the app quits. A Store is safe for use from any goroutine.

Changes other programs make to the file are seen while the store has watchers ([`Store.Watch`](#func-store-watch), [`UseSetting`](#func-usesetting)): the file is read again and merged key by key, and the watchers of the keys that changed run. For a key both sides changed, this process's change not yet written wins (it is written a moment later); otherwise the file's value wins. A write reads the file first and merges it the same way, so it never drops a key another program wrote.

#### func OpenStore

```go
func OpenStore(path string) (*Store, error)
```

OpenStore opens the store kept in the JSON file at path (created at the first write, with its folder). Opening the same path again returns the same Store. A missing file is an empty store. A file that cannot be read or parsed gives an error, but the store is still returned and usable: it starts empty, and a file that did not parse is renamed to path + ".corrupt" before the first write replaces it, so nothing the user had is lost. A file that exists but cannot be read (permissions, a sharing violation, an I/O error) is never overwritten: the store works in memory, each write tries to read the file again (and merges it with the changes made meanwhile once it can), and [`Store.Flush`](#func-store-flush) returns the error until then.

**Example**

A store of the app's own, in its state folder.

```go
dir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "store")
defer os.RemoveAll(dir)

s, err := desktop.OpenStore(filepath.Join(dir, "recent.json"))
if err != nil {
    fmt.Println(err)
    return
}
_ = s.Set("recent", []string{"groceries.md", "ideas.md"})
var recent []string
s.Get("recent", &recent)
fmt.Println(recent)
_ = s.Flush()
// Output: [groceries.md ideas.md]
```

#### func Settings

```go
func Settings() *Store
```

Settings returns the app's settings store, the file settings.json in [`ConfigDir`](#func-configdir). It never returns nil: when the folder cannot be found, the store lives in memory for this run, and when the file cannot be read or parsed it starts empty (see [`OpenStore`](#func-openstore)); [`Store.Err`](#func-store-err) says why.

```go
var s struct{ Theme string; FontSize int }
desktop.Settings().Get("editor", &s)
```

Components read settings with [`UseSetting`](#func-usesetting), which also builds them again when the value changes.

#### func (*Store) Delete

```go
func (s *Store) Delete(key string)
```

Delete removes key and its value; its watchers run.

#### func (*Store) Err

```go
func (s *Store) Err() error
```

Err returns the error of the last failed read or write of the file, nil when the last one succeeded.

#### func (*Store) Flush

```go
func (s *Store) Flush() error
```

Flush writes the changes still in memory now. It is called by itself shortly after a change and when tela.Run returns; call it before a program that does not use tela.Run exits. A store in memory does nothing.

#### func (*Store) Get

```go
func (s *Store) Get(key string, ptr any) bool
```

Get decodes the value of key into ptr, a non-nil pointer (as json.Unmarshal does), and reports whether it did. A missing key, or a value that does not decode into ptr's type, leaves \*ptr as it was and returns false, so a default set before the call stays:

```go
size := 14 // the default
desktop.Settings().Get("fontSize", &size)
```

The stored value is decoded over a copy of \*ptr: a struct field the stored value does not have keeps the one \*ptr had, while slices, arrays and maps the stored value has are replaced whole, and their elements start empty (a key removed from a stored map does not come back from the default, nor does a field an element omits through "omitempty"). \*ptr (a default's slice or map included) is never modified in place, and is assigned only when the call returns true.

#### func (*Store) Has

```go
func (s *Store) Has(key string) bool
```

Has reports whether key has a value.

#### func (*Store) Keys

```go
func (s *Store) Keys() []string
```

Keys returns the keys that have a value, sorted.

#### func (*Store) Path

```go
func (s *Store) Path() string
```

Path returns the file the store is kept in ("" for a store in memory).

#### func (*Store) Set

```go
func (s *Store) Set(key string, v any) error
```

Set stores v under key. It returns an error, and changes nothing, when v cannot be encoded as JSON (a func, a channel). Setting a value equal to the stored one (the same JSON) does nothing; otherwise the watchers of key run, and the file is written shortly after.

#### func (*Store) Watch

```go
func (s *Store) Watch(key string, f func(key string)) (stop func())
```

Watch calls f after each change of key's value (Set with a different value, Delete, another program's write to the file), or of any key when key is "", until stop is called. f runs on the goroutine that made the change (the store's watcher goroutine for another program's), after it, without the store's lock: it may read the store and set values. In components, use [`UseSetting`](#func-usesetting), which builds them again on change.

### type Tray

```go
type Tray struct {
    // Icon is the tray image, the same picture at one or more sizes (16,
    // 24 and 32 pixels cover the usual trays; the OS picks). Required.
    Icon []image.Image
    // Template makes Icon a template image on macOS: only its alpha
    // counts, and the menu bar tints it (dark on a light bar, light on a
    // dark one, inverted while its menu is open), as the system's own
    // status icons are drawn. Draw it as a black silhouette on
    // transparency. Other platforms ignore it and show Icon's colors, so
    // pick a color that reads on light and dark panels, or set Template
    // only on a Mac (runtime.GOOS == "darwin") with a colored icon
    // elsewhere.
    Template bool
    // Tooltip is shown when the pointer rests on the icon.
    Tooltip string
    // Menu is the icon's context menu (a right click; on some Linux
    // panels any click). Empty: no menu.
    Menu []MenuItem
    // OnClick runs when the user clicks the icon (Windows, KDE; some
    // Linux panels open the menu instead and never report a click).
    OnClick func()
    // OnError receives the error when the icon cannot be shown or
    // updated. Nil reports it as a dev warning.
    OnError func(err error)
}
```

Tray is a component that shows an icon in the system tray while it is mounted (the Windows notification area, the StatusNotifierItem host of KDE, GNOME with the AppIndicator extension, and most Linux panels), updates it when its fields change, and removes it when it unmounts. It renders nothing where it is declared; put it anywhere in the app:

```go
func (n Notes) Build() tela.Node {
    win := tela.UseWindow()
    muted, setMuted := tela.UseState(false)
    return Div(
        desktop.Tray{
            Icon:    appIcon, // []image.Image at 16, 24 and 32 px
            Tooltip: "Notes",
            OnClick: func() { win.Show() },
            Menu: []desktop.MenuItem{
                {Label: "Show Notes", OnSelect: func() { win.Show() }},
                {Label: "Mute reminders", Checkbox: true, Checked: muted,
                    OnSelect: func() { setMuted.Set(!muted) }},
                {Separator: true},
                {Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
            },
        },
        // ...the window's content
    )
}
```

With App.OnClose hiding the main window (OnClose: func(w tela.WindowHandle) { w.Hide() }), the app keeps running in the tray. Not every desktop has a tray: when the icon cannot be shown, OnError receives an error wrapping [`ErrUnsupported`](#variables) (GNOME without the AppIndicator extension); then do not hide the window on close, or the app cannot be reached. tela snapshot and windowless trees show no tray. Tests read the tray with telatest's App.Tray and click it with App.ClickTray and App.ClickTrayItem.

**Example**

An app that lives in the tray: closing the window hides it, and the tray's menu shows it again or quits.

```go
icon := []image.Image{image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 16, 16)), image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 32, 32))}
notes := tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    win := tela.UseWindow()
    trayOK, setTrayOK := tela.UseState(true)
    return Div(
        desktop.Tray{
            Icon:    icon,
            Tooltip: "Notes",
            OnClick: func() { win.Show() },
            OnError: func(error) { setTrayOK.Set(false) },
            Menu: []desktop.MenuItem{
                {Label: "Show Notes", OnSelect: func() { win.Show() }},
                {Separator: true},
                {Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
            },
        },
        If(!trayOK, Text("The tray is not available: closing the window quits.")),
    )
})
_ = tela.App{
    Title:   "Notes",
    Root:    notes,
    OnClose: func(w tela.WindowHandle) { w.Hide() }, // keep running in the tray
}
```

#### func (Tray) Build

```go
func (t Tray) Build() tela.Node
```

Build shows the icon while the component is mounted (see [`Tray`](#type-tray)).
